newsitem.title: EGYPT: HSBC sees Cairo market stabilising at 370/375.
newsitem.headline: HSBC sees Cairo market stabilising at 370/375.

text.p: HSBC James Capel disputed on Monday bearish remarks on the Egyptian stock market by rivals ING Barings and said it expected the all-share index to stabilise at between 370 and 375 points.
The index closed at a one-month low of 392.72 on Sunday after hitting an all-time high of 427.77 points on February 24.

The head of the Middle East and North Africa division at ING Barings, Angus Blair, told a conference in Cairo last week that Egypt was now the most expensive emerging market in the world and he would advise investors to take some profits.

But Albert Momdjian, who holds the same position at HSBC James Capel, told Reuters: "Contrary to what others are saying, that the market is expensive, we are still extremely positive on Egypt. We're still buying some stocks. We were taking profits on some, but not at the moment."
"We had a certain overheating and we needed this correction but the market will consolidate at 370/375," he added.

Momdjian said nothing had changed in the macroeconomic fundamentals to justify pulling out of the market. Inflation is down to about five percent, interest rates are coming down, the government deficit is very low, the Egyptian pound has strengthened and tourism is booming, he noted.
"Egypt is the regional market and so any foreign fund needs to have a big exposure to Egypt. P/E ratios went up to around 18 but now we are at 16, which is a decent level.
"We are entering a new phase where we are going to do stock-picking, not buying the market as a whole. There is some readjustment of portfolios but no outflow of funds.
"We're not seeing people rushing out. We have brought long-term investors to the market and there is no reason to panic. It remains a very interesting market," he said.
One factor likely to support the market was the presence of $300 million from dedicated country funds, he added.
Underlining its interest, HSBC James Capel plans to open a brokerage and an investment office in Cairo, he said.
